labels.label: theo:backward_policy
labels.notes: Unmarked, partial: correct. I checked the Lean against l.731-739, l.744-745, l.225-234, l.161 and l.216-222. (1) IsBackwardPolicy (BackwardPolicy.lean:92) is l.745 as printed, with the tensor of l.158: int_{y in Y} B(y)(X) dF_in = int_{x in X} pi(x)(Y) dF_out, where F_in = F_out.bind pi (l.743). isBackwardPolicy_iff_ae_eq_rnDeriv is l.744 with l.745 substituted. It is also brunswic2024theory's notion. In the archived copy (papers/nonacyclic/legacy/orig/931_non_acyclic_gflownets.pdf), Prop. 1(a) sets N_F(., A) := dF(., A)/dF_out. Applied to the transposed edge flow F^T(Y, X) = F_out (x) pi(X x Y), whose out-marginal is F_in, that is exactly l.744-745. The predicate is not trivial: printed_backward_policy_false refutes it for a concrete kernel. (2) backward_policy (l.411) holds on any measurable space and for any lam. Its hypotheses: Phi_i : S =~m S; J_i measurable with Phi_i_* lam = J_i lam; IsEGFPolicy (alpha measurable, nonnegative, summing to 1); f_out measurable; F a GenerativeFlow (pi Markov, F_out finite, l.161) with F_out = f_out lam. Its conclusions: F_in = f_in lam; the printed B* is a backward policy; its weights sum to 1 F_in-a.e.; it is unique setwise F_in-a.e. No conclusion is hidden in a structure, and the hypotheses are inhabited (cx_lebesgue, cx_rnDeriv_reading). Phi_i_* lam = J_i lam is exactly what the change of variables at l.754 uses. The closer's correction of the planner's [r] is right: the condition is Phi_i_* lam << lam, not (Phi_i^{-1})_* lam << lam. The measurability of alpha is the mild condition already discussed in T-egf-headline AUDIT-1 finding (a); I do not raise it again. (3) The instances. backward_policy_addHaar and _diffeomorph take a Haar measure on a finite-dimensional real normed space, measurable bijections with differentiable inverse (resp. C^n diffeomorphisms, n >= 1), and J = coordJac = |det D(Phi^{-1})| (l.233). That is at least the body's setting (R^d, Lebesgue, diffeomorphisms, l.225-234): weaker hypotheses and stronger conclusions. backward_policy_rnDeriv and _equiv_addHaar take lam sigma-finite (automatic for the finite lam of l.161) and quasi-invariant, with J = d(Phi_* lam)/dlam. That is at least the paper's statement under the lam-Jacobian reading. None of them is >= the printed appendix statement in its printed reading (lam << Lebesgue, coordinate Jacobian), because that statement is false. So partial and unmarked, with Q1 asking which form is of record, is correct. (4) The core question. Both witnesses meet every clause printed at l.731-732, plus the standing assumptions of l.161. R is a Polish differential manifold. lam is finite (proved for lamAc and lamCx) and << Lebesgue (lamCx is even equivalent to it). The Phi_i are translations, hence diffeomorphisms; the Lean records their differentiable inverses. alpha lies in the simplex (IsEGFPolicy, proved). F_out = f_out lam is finite and pi is Markov. No regularity of f_out is printed. The witnesses violate only clauses of def:egf that the appendix sentence does not repeat. One is topological ergodicity (l.221): the orbits x + Z are discrete. The other is 'Riemannian manifold with its volume' (l.217), which the appendix replaces by lam << Lebesgue. Under the literal l.731-732 definition, the witnesses are faithful refutations, not strawmen. printed_inflow_not_ac refutes l.737: F_in is singular to lam, so F_in != g lam for every g. printed_backward_policy_false refutes l.735-737 with the coordinate Jacobian of l.230. By hand, on [0,1) the true weights are (2/3, 1/3) against the printed (1/2, 1/2), and the true dF_in/dlam is 3/4 against the printed 1. Suppose 'an EGF' imports def:egf's ergodicity. Then the formal witnesses do not apply, but both findings survive by analogs I checked by hand (not formalized). For finding 1: on R, Phi = (x+1, x-sqrt2), alpha = (1/2,1/2), lam = 1_[0,1) Leb, f_out = 1. The forward words x + m - n*sqrt2 are dense, and F_in lives on [1,2) and [-sqrt2, 1-sqrt2), so it is singular to lam. An arc on the circle with an irrational rotation also works. For finding 2, the closer's circle sketch is correct: printed weights (1/2,1/2), true weights rho(s)/(rho(s)+rho(s-theta)), equal a.e. iff rho is theta-invariant, hence constant. Suppose instead that def:egf's Riemannian volume is imported in place of lam << Lebesgue. Then finding 1 vanishes, since a volume is quasi-invariant under diffeomorphisms, as the REPORT itself says. Finding 2 survives only for the coordinate reading. A smooth analog: lam = e^{-x^2} Leb, the volume of g = e^{-2x^2} dx^2; Phi = (id, x+1), alpha = (1/2,1/2), f_out = 1; the printed f_in is 1 and the true one is (1 + e^{2s-1})/2. The Riemannian Jacobian, however, is the lam-Jacobian, and with it the statement holds. So the REPORT's findings are true as written. Two places need a precision (minor findings 1-2). (5) Findings 4-6 are true. |J| appears at l.228, l.736-737 and l.754-764, against |det J| at l.233. \end{proof} is at l.758, before the deduction at l.759-766, and the ledger's proof_span is [740, 758]. beta^i divides by f_in, and the 0-convention sits on an F_in-null set. Questions Q1-Q3 are genuine readings and are reported as kb/0011 requires.

findings.where: scaffold/EGFScaffold/BackwardPolicy.lean:12-14 (module: 'false in its setting'), :61-70 (SCOPE), :756-761 (printed_backward_policy_false docstring), :835-839 (printed_inflow_not_ac docstring); REPORT findings[2]
findings.what: Neither formal witness is topologically ergodic: the groups generated by {id, x+1} and by {x+1} have discrete orbits x + Z. The Lean file says the statement is 'false in its setting' without saying that this setting is l.731-732 read without def:egf's ergodicity clause (l.221). This file will graduate and be cited. REPORT findings[2] discloses the point, but only for the coordinate-Jacobian finding. It gives no ergodic analog for finding 1 (F_in not << lam), the one Q2 asks the author to rule on. The finding is not false: the appendix's definition carries no ergodicity, and ergodic analogs exist (see the label notes).
findings.fix: In the SCOPE and in both finding docstrings, add: 'the witnesses meet l.731-732 and l.161 but are not topologically ergodic (def:egf, l.221); ergodic analogs exist (not formalized)'. In REPORT findings[2], add the analog for finding 1: on R, Phi = (x+1, x-sqrt2), alpha = (1/2,1/2), lam = 1_[0,1) Leb, f_out = 1. Forward words are dense and F_in is singular to lam. An arc on the circle with an irrational rotation also works. Optionally, formalize one ergodic witness.

findings.what: printed_inflow_not_ac refutes l.737 (the inflow density) and l.759's 'F_in (x) B(. -> X) << lam'. It does not refute the B* display (l.735-736). Its own witness has p = 1, alpha = 1, f_out = 1. There the printed weight is beta^1 = 1 wherever the term lies in (0, infinity). So with the coordinate Jacobian (J = 1), the printed B*(s) = delta_{s-1} is the backward policy. By hand, both sides of l.745 equal Leb{x in X cap [0,1) : x+1 in Y}. findings[0] and the Lean docstring (l.838-839, 'the printed formula for f_in fails for every choice of the Jacobian factor J') are precise. The two summary phrases are not, and would tell the author that the backward-policy formula fails under lam << Lebesgue for every Jacobian.
findings.fix: In hypotheses[1] and questions[1], write 'the f_in line (l.737) fails for every reading of the Jacobian'. Optionally add that in this witness the B* line holds.

findings.where: REPORT labels[0].findings[1], last sentence; scaffold/EGFScaffold/BackwardPolicy.lean:67-68 (SCOPE: 'for every quasi-invariant lam')
findings.what: (a) 'Every application in the paper takes lambda Lebesgue, Haar or a Riemannian volume, where the two readings agree.' On a Riemannian manifold a coordinate Jacobian depends on the chart. The two readings agree for the Jacobian in orthonormal frames, or in charts where lam is Lebesgue (flat tori). For the sphere rotations of l.819 they agree because both are 1 in the Riemannian sense, not in arbitrary charts. A smooth Riemannian volume on which the coordinate reading fails exists: lam = e^{-x^2} Leb, the volume of e^{-2x^2} dx^2 on R. (b) The SCOPE's 'for every quasi-invariant lam' omits a condition. backward_policy_rnDeriv assumes SigmaFinite lam (automatic for the finite lam of l.161), and backward_policy needs a J with Phi_* lam = J lam.
findings.fix: (a) Write 'where the two readings agree when the Jacobian is taken in orthonormal frames (charts in which lam is Lebesgue)'. (b) Write 'every sigma-finite quasi-invariant lam'.
